children: Any rise in the U.S. dollar could be limited, Commerzbank's Thu Lan Nguyen says in a note. The dollar edges lower Monday following strong gains on Friday after Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh hinted at a possible rate rise due to inflation concerns. A September rate rise is "by no means a done deal," Nguyen says. "I would be cautious about jumping on the dollar euphoria too quickly." Ahead of September's meeting will be Friday's U.S. jobs data, where another weak figure could "trigger a significant [dollar] correction." Inflation figures are also due next week. Inflation data recently "have hardly been a cause for alarm," she says. The DXY dollar index falls 0.1% to 99.619, having hit a two-week high of 99.726 on Friday. (jessica.fleetham@wsj.com)
